case_title: Jayedeepsinh Pravinsinh Chavda & Ors. v. State of Gujarat
accused_victim_relationship: Spouse (husband, appellant no.1); in-laws (appellant nos. 2 and 3)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.306 (abetment of suicide); IPC s.498A (cruelty); IPC s.114
evidence_type: Witness statements (informant, other witnesses, victim's cousins); FIR; investigating officer's chargesheet findings
trial_court_outcome: Discharge application under s.227 CrPC dismissed; charges framed under ss.306 and 498A IPC
high_court_outcome: Criminal revision dismissed (order dated 09.05.2024); charges under ss.306 and 498A upheld
neutral_facts: The victim had been married to the accused for about twelve years and lived in the matrimonial home with the victim's in-laws. No child was born in the first five years of the marriage, and the victim was allegedly subjected to physical and mental harassment on that account, leading to a return to the parental home for a time. After the victim returned to the matrimonial home, a son was born. About twelve months before the death, the victim told the victim's father that the accused had sold gold ornaments the victim had received as streedhan at the marriage. When the victim demanded their return, the victim was allegedly physically and mentally harassed. On 18 April 2021 the victim's father was informed that the victim had died by hanging. It was alleged that the harassment by the accused compelled the victim to take the victim's own life. An FIR was registered on the same day at the victim's father's instance. The investigation produced the FIR, the investigating officer's chargesheet findings, and statements of the victim's father, other witnesses and the victim's cousins. These described repeated complaints by the victim of physical and mental harassment by the accused, including the sale of the ornaments and harassment on demand for their return. The cousins' statements mentioned only incidents that occurred about a year before the death.
offence_severity: Maximum ten years' imprisonment and fine (s.306 IPC); minimum not stated
physical_harm: Death of the victim by hanging (suicide), as alleged
financial_property_loss: Gold ornaments (streedhan) allegedly sold by the accused (alleged)
motive: alleged: harassment over the accused's sale of the victim's streedhan gold ornaments and the victim's demands for their return; the Court found no intention to instigate suicide
key_evidence_accepted: FIR; Investigating Officer's chargesheet findings; statements of the informant, other witnesses and victim's cousins (accepted prima facie for s.498A)
witness_credibility: No definitive credibility finding; prima facie reliance on consistent statements; lack of complaints over twelve years not treated as disproving cruelty
trial_duration: offence: 18.04.2021; trial judgment: 28.02.2024 (Sessions Court discharge order); High Court: 09.05.2024; Supreme Court: 10.12.2024
legal_representation: Appellants: Tejas Barot, Sr. Adv., with Shamik Shirishbhai Sanjanwala, Ms. Rhea Chokshi, Aditya Tripathi, Advs. Respondent (State of Gujarat): Ms. Swati Ghildiyal, Ms. Devyani Bhatt, Ms. Neha Singh, Advs.
investigation_status: FIR registered 18.04.2021; chargesheet filed; charges framed under ss.306 and 498A IPC
appeal_history: Trial court (Sessions): discharge application dismissed 28.02.2024. High Court: criminal revision dismissed 09.05.2024. Supreme Court: appeal partly allowed; discharged from s.306, s.498A charge upheld
defence_argument: Allegations baseless and concocted; no material showing involvement in abetment; mens rea under s.306 absent; allegations vague and general, not constituting s.306 or s.498A offences; only one instance of harassment, about a year before death
legal_principle_applied: s.306 requires clear mens rea and a positive, direct or proximate act of instigation or aid; mere harassment is insufficient. s.498A requires cruelty or harassment by husband or relatives, prima facie assessed at charge stage
precedent_relied_upon: U. Suvetha v. State (2009) 6 SCC 757; State of A.P. v. M. Madhusudhan Rao (2008) 15 SCC 582; S.S. Chheena v. Vijay Kumar Mahajan (2010) 12 SCC 190; Ramesh Kumar v. State of Chhattisgarh (2001) 9 SCC 618; M. Mohan v. State (2011) 3 SCC 626; Amalendu Pal alias Jhantu v. State of West Bengal (2010) 1 SCC 707; Kamalakar v. State of Karnataka (2007 SCC OnLine Kar 824); Ude Singh v. State of Haryana (2019) 17 SCC 301
other_sentence_order: Trial under s.498A IPC to proceed against the accused; pending applications disposed of
